data_status: REAL DATA - DAIAD smart water meters (Alicante, Spain), aggregated by TANKCAST
target_unit: litres per meter per hour (mean over the meters that reported in that hour)
feature_policy: Calendar features for the forecast time plus lags/rolling statistics of the target that are at least `horizon` steps old. No temperature or occupancy features are used.

preprocessing.missing_policy: missing time steps are left empty; rows lacking any needed history are dropped (no imputation)

metric_explanation.MAE: Mean Absolute Error: the average size of the forecast error, in the target's own unit. Easy to read.
metric_explanation.RMSE: Root Mean Squared Error: like MAE but squares errors first, so rare large misses count more. RMSE is always >= MAE; a big gap between them means occasional large errors.
metric_explanation.persistence: Baseline: predicts that demand equals its value `horizon` steps earlier (at a 24-hour horizon this is simply 'same hour yesterday').
metric_explanation.seasonal_naive: Baseline: predicts the value from the same time in the previous cycle (e.g. same hour yesterday).

dataset_limitations: Residential households in Spain, not a hostel or an Indian city; usage patterns and climate differ.
Values are per meter, not per building. Scaling to a hostel needs an explicit, separate assumption.
If a meter skipped readings, its next 'litres since last reading' may cover several hours but is counted in one hour.
No temperature or occupancy data is included.
limitations: Metrics come from ONE chronological test period; they say little about other seasons or conditions.
The test period was not used for tuning, but only fixed hyper-parameters were tried.
Predictions are in the dataset's unit and scale; they are not hostel demand unless the data is.
